changes: p2: 'varman' moved from the name to titles (name 'Candraśaṃśerajaṅga'). Title normalised to 'pradhānāmātya'. Roles minister + relative_only kept: he was Prime Minister in VS 1979 and is named to identify his son.

p3: 'varman' moved to titles (name 'Kesarasaṃśera'). Role 'owner' removed: the colophon says only that he searched for and collected the palm-leaf exemplar, not that this copy belongs to him. Role 'other' kept (collector of the exemplar).

p4: 'śarman' moved from the name to titles (name 'Hemarāja'). Title given as 'rājaguru' (Nepālarājaguru). Commissioner role kept because he had the copy made through a scribe (lekhakadvārā saṃlekhya).
Purpose rewritten as a paraphrase; 'saumanasyātha' is read as an error for 'saumanasyāya'.
Notes: added the exemplar date (saṃvat 092, probably NS = c. 972 CE) and the unnamed hired scribe; recorded that the catalogue's 'scribe' field conflicts with the colophon.

purpose: for the lasting delight of the learned (cirāya sumanasāṃ saumanasyāya)
notes: The copy is dated VS 1979, which is about 1922/23 CE. This fits both Tribhuvana's reign (1911–55) and Candra Śamśera's term as Prime Minister (1901–29). It was copied from an old palm-leaf manuscript dated 'saṃvat 092', which Kesara Śamśera (Kaiser Shumsher), third son of Candra Śamśera, had searched for and collected. The era of that date is not given, but it is very probably NS 92, about 972 CE. That is the exemplar's date, not this copy's. The catalogue gives Hemarāja Śarman as scribe, but the colophon says he had the text written out 'through a scribe' (lekhakadvārā saṃlekhya). He is therefore the commissioner/editor, and the actual copyist is not named. 'saumanasyātha' looks like an error for 'saumanasyāya'. 'rājagurū' should read 'rājaguru'. 'kesarasaṃśera' is a spelling of Kesaraśaṃśera.
